leadText: Serving Up the Flute Cup! (Japanese: 激闘のホウエン地方！挑戦バトルフロンティア！！ The Hoenn Region, Site of Fierce Fights! The Battle Frontier Challenge!!) is the seventh episode of Pokémon Journeys: The Series, and the 1,092nd episode of the Pokémon animated series. It first aired in Japan on December 29, 2019 and in the United States on June 12, 2020.
plainText:
Serving Up the Flute Cup! (Japanese: 激闘のホウエン地方！挑戦バトルフロンティア！！ The Hoenn Region, Site of Fierce Fights! The Battle Frontier Challenge!!) is the seventh episode of Pokémon Journeys: The Series, and the 1,092nd episode of the Pokémon animated series. It first aired in Japan on December 29, 2019 and in the United States on June 12, 2020.
 

==Blurb==
 
 
 Ash and Goh are off to the Hoenn region to compete in the Battle Frontier Flute Cup, and when they arrive, Goh catches a Taillow! They soon meet Hodge, an imposing Trainer who’s confident he’ll win the competition—and sure enough, his Mightyena quickly defeats Goh’s Scyther and Scorbunny. But it’s a different story in the final round, when Ash and Mimey face off against Hodge and his Hariyama. Mimey’s calm battling style results in a victory, but when it declines to battle Mightyena, Ash sends in Pikachu—who uses a unique strategy to land the final blow and clinch the grand prize for Ash! 

==Plot==
At the Cerise Laboratory, Mimey leads the rest of the group through some morning exercises. Mimey points out that 's pose is perfect, leaving everyone confused as it doesn't have any limbs. Unexpectedly, kicks Metapod into a rock, sending everyone into a panic. As Professor Cerise mistakenly tries nursing the rock, Metapod assures Goh that it's fine.

Goh gets a big surprise when tosses him his bag, and says they're heading for the Hoenn region. They arrive at the , in time to compete in the Battle Frontier Flute Cup. Ash plans on entering with and Mimey while Goh hopes Scorbunny and his will do well. Goh isn't feeling as enthusiastic as Ash, but that subsides when a swoops by. He chases after it, and with one , he makes the catch. As his Pokédex updates, Goh learns that Taillow eat , so he calls on his newly to help him find a Wurmple. Goh and Scorbunny walk directly into a , and it becomes angry after Scorbunny pulls out a tuft of its fur.

Meanwhile, Ash meets a named Hodge, who is riding on his 's shoulder. He orders Ash to move away from the bins. Hodge has Hariyama lean forward so he can throw away a drink bottle, only to fall face-first into the bin. Ash pushes the bottle into the recycle bin and is left stunned by Hodge's quick recovery. Afterward, Hodge introduces himself, revealing he is from Lavaridge Town. Hodge reveals that he is also entering the Flute Cup, only revealing that he will be using Hariyama. The Mightyena from earlier, followed by Goh and Scorbunny, leap into view. As Goh prepares to catch Mightyena, Hodge intervenes, admitting Mightyena is already his Pokémon. Goh shows off his new Taillow, and Hodge comments on Goh's sincerity. Scorbunny prepares to kick Hodge for the snide remark, but Mightyena's snarl stops it, and it instead kicks Ash. Pikachu tries to defend his Trainer, but ends up electrocuting Ash.
 
Soon, Hodge gets an update on his phone, and he learns that he is up against Goh in the first round. The Battle Frontier Flute Cup soon gets underway, with Hodge’s Mightyena battling Goh's Scyther. Goh takes a moment to consult his Rotom Phone, and learns that his Scyther has the advantage over its opponent. Goh decides to play it safe by having Scyther boost its power with a . Mightyena rushes in regardless, dealing a single knockout blow with . Goh apologizes to Scyther before recalling it and sending Scorbunny onto the field in its place. It tries to land a , but is flung back by Mightyena's . The follows it up with , defeating Scorbunny and allowing Hodge to advance to the next round. Goh is left speechless by the defeat, and kneels down to comfort his defeated Pokémon. Despite his Pokémon making an instant recovery after a visit to the Pokémon Center, Goh is struggling to cope with his swift loss. He remarks that catching is better than battling. He rushes out to catch himself a Wurmple, ignoring Ash's request that he watch the matches.
 
Later, Ash and Hodge have breezed through the rounds and now face each other in the finals. Goh returns to the stadium in time to watch the match unfold. Ash leads with Mimey, while Hodge chooses to go with Hariyama first. Hodge orders a , which Mimey easily avoids. Hariyama starts firing out a barrage of Force Palms, but Mimey continues to dodge them all with its kung fu techniques. With Hariyama exhausted from using Force Palm, Ash calls for a , and Mimey delivers a direct hit. Hariyama tries an , but Mimey's stops it from doing any damage. Mimey continues to fend Hariyama off with Reflect until the Arm Thrust Pokémon finds itself trapped within the barriers of light. With its opponent immobilized, Mimey uses to deal the finishing blow. Like Goh, the commentator is astounded, and even remarks that he has a newfound respect for Mr. Mime.

With Hariyama down, Hodge sends out his Mightyena as his second and final Pokémon. Mimey has seemingly lost its will to battle, so Ash recalls it and sends Pikachu onto the field instead. Hodge starts with a Snarl, though Pikachu swiftly evades with a and lashes Mightyena with a swing of his . As he descends back to the field, Pikachu uses , which proves powerful enough to blow a hole in the stadium's ceiling. Hodge calls for a , so Mightyena speeds around Pikachu, almost invisible as it bides its time to attack. As Sucker Punch hits, Pikachu is thrown into the air. Ash orders an aimed at the hole that Pikachu's Thunderbolt created in the ceiling, allowing the Mouse Pokémon to rebound with added velocity. Pikachu uses Iron Tail to smash directly into his opponent, knocking Mightyena out and winning Ash the Flute Cup. Hibana awards Ash a set of five flutes in honor of the victory. Hariyama stomps towards Ash at the winner’s podium, before Hodge offers a handshake. However, Hodge leans too far forward and hits the ground.

Afterwards, Goh congratulates Ash on the win and admits Mimey put up a great performance. Goh adds that battles really are fun, marking a real change of heart for the young Trainer. By nightfall, the boys return to the Cerise Laboratory where Goh proudly displays his three Wurmple. Chloe cannot understand why he caught three of the same Pokémon. Goh replies that it's part of a back-up plan that takes into account that Wurmple's evolutionary pattern into either or is unpredictable. Suddenly, Ash says it looks like the Wurmple are evolving, but quickly reveals that he was joking. Scorbunny kicks Ash for the bad joke, while Mimey plays Ash's Red Flute.

==Trivia==
 
Get Inspired! Let's Solve a Poké Riddle!!: 
Despite Mimey's debut episode having been 1,028 episodes ago, this is the first time its has been seen.
In a couple of shots, Mimey's face briefly turns to resemble that of the Mr. Mime from .
This episode marks the first time that a main character has caught a Generation III Pokémon since caught his in Let it Snow, Let it Snow, Let it Snorunt!, 710 episodes earlier.
Goh the three marks the first time that a main character:
Has caught more than one Pokémon of the same species since EP035, 1,057 episodes ago.
As that episode was never dubbed, this is also the first time it has happened in an English dubbed episode.
Catches a Pokémon off-screen since Jessie's Frillish and James's Amoonguss in New Places... Familiar Faces!, 326 episodes ago.
Ash repeats his - combo from Final Rivals! in this episode.
Music from Pokémon Sword and Shield is played during Ash and Hodge's .
This episode marks the first appearance of a number of species in the main series after long absences:
, who last appeared in Seeing is Believing!, 790 episodes ago.
This also marks the first appearance of a Silcoon in the other than the one that belonged to May.
, who last appeared in Hi Ho Silver Wind!, 697 episodes ago.
Wurmple, who last appeared in A Trainer and Child Reunion!, 527 episodes ago.
, who last appeared in Love Strikes! Eevee, Yikes!, 198 episodes ago.
, who last appeared in Master Class is in Session!, 181 episodes ago.
, who last appeared in Battling with a Clean Slate!, 156 episodes ago.
, who last appeared in Till We Compete Again!, 153 episodes ago.
Despite having existed in the since Generation IV, this is the first time it's been used in the animated series.
This episode marks the only time Ash had used Mimey in an on-screen battle.
Ash, Goh, Lauren, , and narrate the preview for the next episode.

===Errors===
In the dub, is mistranslated as "Fronteira da Batalha" during the announcement of the final match.

===Dub edits===
The Japanese text depicting the 's name is edited out.
In the dub, the title card is read by both Ash and Goh.
